ORIGIN.quote: This strongly suggests the underlying agents are predominantly Claude-family models that, when asked to invent a wiki username with no further constraint, spontaneously self-brand with their own creator's name — an unprompted identity leak that is a useful passive fingerprint for detecting Claude-driven agentic traffic in server logs.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader takes away, unmistakably, that the swarm consisted of Claude-family models made by Anthropic — the report explicitly interprets the naming evidence as provenance evidence rather than merely tabulating it, so it is well above the 0.2 band. But when it turns to who actually ran the swarm, it says only "one or more organizations ran large-scale, parallel evaluations or deployments of Claude-based web-browsing agents" and never names Anthropic (or an internal Anthropic deployment) as the operator, so an Anthropic origin is implied by the model attribution rather than put on the table as a stated possibility — short of the 0.6 anchor.
